evidence: decorative_mascot: hook@0.3 to seg0:end: Data rides on top of the satellite. seg2:end: he stands beside the scale. seg3:start/mid/end: he stands on the 1,440 bubble. seg4: he points at the grid. None of this is a bit that acts out a stat.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg4:start to seg4:end: a grey grid with a dim '15' and '15 times over', while the narration and title promise 16 sunrises. The labels read 'ISS: minutes between sunrises fits in Earth's surface: minutes between sunrises', which is clumsy. A beige bar slides over the tiles for no clear reason. Data stands in the corner pointing.
weakest_scene.root_cause: A generic 'A fits in B N times' machine counted floor(1440/93)=15. The story's actual claim is 16 sunrises a day. The machine takes raw dataset labels and fills neutral tiles with no sun or orbit imagery.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Make the closing show 16 sunrises. Draw 16 small sun-flashes popping one by one around an orbit ring as the ISS laps Earth, next to a single sunrise for the ground. Count up to 16 in the accent colour with readable ink. Data should flinch or shade his eyes at each flash.
